rest = time when you are not active so the body can recover
diet = the food you usually eat; also eating less to lose weight
obese = very overweight in a way that is bad for health
underweight = weighing less than is healthy
get fit = to become healthier and stronger through exercise
addiction = when you cannot stop a harmful habit
smoking = breathing in smoke from cigarettes
give up smoking = to stop using cigarettes
alcohol = drinks such as beer or wine that can make you drunk
drunk = having had too much alcohol
drugs = illegal substances, or medicine in some contexts
hygiene = keeping yourself and things clean to stay healthy
wash your hands = to clean your hands with soap and water
brush your hair = to pull a brush through your hair
fill a tooth = when a dentist repairs a hole in a tooth
braces = wires that a dentist uses to straighten teeth
dentist chair = the special chair you sit in at the dentist
blood test = when a nurse takes blood to check your health
sick note = a paper from a parent or doctor that explains an absence
stay in bed = to rest in bed because you are ill
